questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The first astronauts to land on the Moon
The deep ocean and the strange life found there
Famous sea monsters in old stories and films
How volcanoes on land are formed and studied
questions.why: Sam says they'll be diving into the deep seas and seeing some of its strange sights.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention photographs from the Apollo mission?
options: To show how small the Moon looks from Earth
To explain how astronauts studied the oceans
To show that the Moon is covered in water
They showed how much of Earth is ocean
questions.why: He says only when we went to the Moon did we really see the size of Earth's oceans and call it the Blue Planet.

questions.q: What are conditions like at the very bottom of the ocean?
options: Dark, very cold and under huge pressure
Warm and bright, with lots of plants
Cold but full of light from the surface
Dark but warm everywhere, like a volcano
questions.why: Neil says no sunlight reaches it, so it's totally dark and extremely cold, with massive pressure.

questions.q: According to Alex Rogers, what is the first problem with hydrothermal vents?
options: They are too hot for cameras to film
They are dangerous for divers to visit
They are hard to find as they're so small
They only exist near the Antarctic coast
questions.why: He says they cover a very small area, so it's 'like trying to find a needle in a haystack'.

questions.q: What did Alex see when his camera reached the vent?
options: Suddenly there was life everywhere
There was nothing living there at all
Only a few small fish swimming slowly
Clouds of smoke that hid everything
questions.why: Life is 'thin on the ground', but then the camera finds 'abundant life all over the sea floor' around the vents.

questions.q: Which creatures are mentioned as living near the vents?
options: Sharks, whales and giant octopuses
Sea turtles, jellyfish and starfish
Penguins, seals and colourful fish
Mussels, tube worms and hairy crabs
questions.why: Neil mentions vent mussels, tube worms and blind 'yeti crabs' with hairy claws.

options: Around 150 years ago
During the Apollo missions
In the 1970s
Only a few years ago
questions.why: Sam says these vents may be as old as Earth itself, but were only discovered in the 1970s.

questions.q: What is Kerry Howell's opinion about the deep sea?
options: Scientists have now found almost everything there
She's sure there's much more to discover
It is too dangerous to explore any further
There is probably no more life down there
questions.why: She says, 'I have absolutely no doubt that there is plenty more to discover down there.'
